description: We’re a creative team passionate about technology, design, innovation, and space exploration. Combining skills in coding, app development, UI/UX, and creative design, we aim to turn ideas into engaging experiences while learning, experimenting, and solving real-world challenges together.
summary:
Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an educational mobile game designed to introduce young learners to space exploration and engineering through interactive missions and challenges. Players take on the role of astronauts, managing essential resources such as oxygen, water, food, and electricity while solving engineering problems and responding to unexpected events.
The project addresses the challenge of making complex space engineering concepts more accessible and engaging for young learners. Instead of only reading scientific information, players actively make decisions, manage interconnected systems, and experience the consequences of their choices. To improve the learning experience, we integrated an interactive chatbot that provides guidance, answers questions, and assists players throughout the game. We also simplified the initial levels to help beginners understand the game mechanics before progressing to more challenging missions.
This project is important because it encourages curiosity about space exploration while developing problem-solving, critical-thinking, decision-making, and resource-management skills. It transforms engineering education into an interactive experience and inspires young learners to explore STEM fields.
details:
Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an educational mobile game that allows players to experience the challenges of managing a space mission. Players complete missions involving life-support systems, oxygen and water management, food production, electrical power, radiation protection, and equipment failures.

The game works through interactive tasks, simulations, decision-making activities, and unexpected mission events. Players must manage limited resources, solve engineering problems, and understand how different systems affect one another. An interactive chatbot is also integrated to provide guidance, answer questions, and assist players throughout their journey. The initial levels are designed to be beginner-friendly, with challenges gradually becoming more advanced.

The project makes space engineering concepts easier to understand through practical and interactive learning. It encourages problem-solving, critical thinking, decision-making, and resource management. It also provides an engaging learning environment where players can explore scientific and engineering concepts at their own pace, with additional guidance from the integrated chatbot.

Our intended impact is to make space engineering and STEM education more accessible and interesting to young learners. We aim to inspire curiosity about space exploration and help students develop engineering thinking by allowing them to solve problems, make decisions, and learn from their consequences. In the future, the game could also support classroom activities and educational programs.

Our project was developed using the following tools and technologies:

  • Figma: Used for user interface and user experience design, including wireframes and visual layouts.
  • Flutter: Used for mobile application development.
  • Dart: The main programming language used to develop the application and its game logic.
  • CustomPainter and Ticker: Used to create 2D graphics, animations, and interactive visual elements.
  • Shared Preferences: Used for local data storage and saving player progress.

The project is software-based and does not require specialized external hardware.

Our creativity comes from combining space education with interactive engineering simulations and gameplay. Instead of presenting scientific concepts through ordinary lessons or quizzes, we allow players to experience realistic engineering challenges in a simplified game environment.

The game also introduces interconnected systems, where one problem can affect several other systems. For example, an electrical failure may affect heating and life-support operations, requiring players to analyze the situation and decide how to respond. The integrated chatbot adds another interactive learning element by providing assistance throughout the missions. Additionally, the gradual difficulty progression helps accommodate beginners while maintaining more challenging experiences for advanced players.

We considered accessibility and affordability during the development process. Since the project is software-based, it does not require expensive physical equipment, specialized laboratory facilities, or additional hardware to experience the main gameplay.

We focused on developing a mobile application with 2D graphics and simplified simulations rather than hardware-intensive environments. This approach helps keep the project more accessible and reduces the need for expensive resources. Local progress storage also supports gameplay without requiring continuous internet access for saving progress. Overall, our goal is to provide an educational experience that can be accessed through commonly available mobile devices while keeping development and usage costs relatively low.
